renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: Clade calls by QC status
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the sequences assigned to a Nextclade clade, split by their overall quality status. It answers which clades the run found and whether the calls rest on good sequences.
    How to read: a clade made of good sequences is a call to trust. Bars that are mostly mediocre or bad mean the clade rests on incomplete or odd sequences, so check the missing bases and the coverage before reporting them.
    Lines and annotations: the colour is the overall QC status, good for a score from 0 to 29, mediocre from 30 to 99 and bad from 100, the bands Nextclade defines for its combined quality score.
    Source: https://docs.nextstrain.org/projects/nextclade/en/stable/user/algorithm/06-quality-control.html
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: clade
    color: qc_overallStatus
    labels:
      clade: Clade
      qc_overallStatus: QC status

- component: card
  title: Genome coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of the reference genome covered by the sequences, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how complete the consensus genomes are.
    How to read: a box piled near one means complete genomes. A long tail towards zero marks sequences with large missing stretches, which weaken both the clade call and the mutation list. Open the table to see which ones.
  column: coverage
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average, with quartiles

- component: table
  title: Clade assignment table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sequence with its clade, the Pango lineage Nextclade assigns, the counts of substitutions, deletions, insertions, frame shifts and missing or ambiguous bases, its coverage and its quality score and status. It answers which sequences need attention and what each one carries.
    How to read: sort by quality status to find the sequences to inspect, then read the missing base count to see whether coverage explains the flag.

- component: card
  title: Clades found
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct clades, with the number of sequences beside it, and the bars rank the clades by how many sequences carry them. It answers how diverse the run is and which clades dominate.
    How to read: one dominant clade is a single outbreak lineage in circulation, several of similar size is a mixed collection. A clade seen once is worth checking for a quality problem before it is reported.
  column: clade
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: clade
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: sequences, by clade
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Missing bases
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of missing bases (N) per sequence, with the lowest and highest value beside it, and the histogram shows how they are spread. It answers how much of each genome the sequencing failed to call.
    How to read: a pile at low values is a clean run. A long tail of sequences with thousands of missing bases is expected for low viral loads or failed amplicons, and these sequences get a worse quality status.
    Source: https://docs.nextstrain.org/projects/nextclade/en/stable/user/output-files/04-results-tsv.html
  column: totalMissing
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: median, with the distribution
